title: Fabrication of guggulsterone-E-integrated chitosan–zinc nanohybrids: surface chemical insights, biointerface interactions and multi-target antidiabetic mechanisms
content: The research focuses on evaluating the potential anti-diabetic efficacy of encapsulating guggulsterone-E extract within chitosan–ZnO NPs (Gu@ChZn NPs) through a sustainable production method. UV-vis, FT-IR, FE-SEM, HR-TEM, EDX, XPS, and XRD characterizations were used to identify the physicochemical properties of the Gu@ChZn NPs. The UV-visible absorption peak was noted at 320 nm, and morphological analysis revealed that the particles were mainly spherical with uneven surface characteristics and sizes of 5–45 nm. Based on the biological evaluation, it was found that compared with guggulsterone-E alone, Gu@ChZn NPs had a greater inhibitory effect on selected enzymes such as lipase, α-glucosidase, and α-amylase. Critical genes related to diabetes, including KCNJ11, TCF7L2, IRS-1, HNF1A, HXK4, and ABCC8, were predicted to interact with guggulsterone-E via network pharmacology. Molecular docking analysis revealed substantial binding affinities, with ABCC8 exhibiting the most significant interaction at −9.07 kcal mol−1. The Gu@ChZn NPs exhibit potential as a promising bio-functional nanocomposite with enhanced enzyme inhibitory properties relevant to diabetes-associated metabolic regulation.
